To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have produced an immortalized human muscle cell line that functions as well as normal myoblasts when transplanted into muscle of immunocompromized animals.
we have developed a protocol for immortalizing normal human myoblastic cells that can be applied to any human muscle disease.

1) human myoblast senescence can be overcome by telomerase and Cdk4; 2) LHCN‐ M2 is a human myogenic line that is capable of regenerating muscle in vivo; and 3) the use of LHCN‐‐M2 cells in the treatment of muscular dystrophies will be a major step towards the development of a gene therapy for these diseases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new cell line that could serve as an alternative to the use of embryonic stem cells for therapeutic purposes in neuromuscular disorders.
the development of immortalized human myoblast cell lines that can be used for therapeutic purposes.
the development of a novel approach for treating muscular dystrophies based on the use of immortal human myogenic cell lines.

the expression of telomerases and cyclin‐D1 in human myoblastic cells allows the production of an immortal cell line that can be used to study the molecular mechanisms of muscular diseases.
the LHCN‐MD cell line is a valuable tool for studying muscle regeneration and the molecular mechanisms of aging, as well as for the development of new therapeutic strategies for muscular diseases.
this is a novel cell model for the study of the molecular and cellular basis of aging and muscle diseases, and a potential tool for gene therapy.

the LHCN‐ M2 myoblast line has been generated, characterized, and tested in an animal model.

the LHCN‐m2 cell line represents an unlimited source of human myogenic cells that can be used as a model for normal and pathological human muscle, and that it is a useful cell line for the development and testing of therapeutic strategies for muscular disorders.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of immortalized human muscle cell lines is an attractive alternative to primary myoblasts for MTT, especially for diseases that affect the adult muscle.
telomerase and Cdk4 expression can overcome cellular aging in normal myoblasts, and thus that telomerase‐expressing myoblasts can be used as universal donor cells for MTT.
the combination of telomerase with a cyclin‐dependent inhibitor is an efficient way to immortalize normal human myogenic cells.
